title: First human blind ratings — the owner on 49 tournament pairs (Wave Q, Workstream A)
definitionOfDone: a real person, blind to every arm, rated real rendered audio through the real Listening Room. Not a fixture, not a simulation.

session.source: docs/evidence/model-tournament-live.json (12 classical PDMX tasks x 3 seeds)
session.rater: the platform owner, blind to arm, seed, task and orientation
session.startedClean: two votes cast by earlier automation were deleted before the session (PR-70)

gateC.reason: 0 independent rater(s) so far; Gate C needs at least 5.
gateC.note: the owner is the session owner, so these 49 votes are recorded and excluded from the Gate C verdict by design. Gate C needs five independent raters.

reading.headline: Not one of the five comparisons is distinguishable from a coin flip. Every two-sided p is >= 0.34 at n = 9-10 with a single rater. This session establishes no ranking, and was never large enough to.
whatItDoesEstablish: The proxy judge’s central claim is not reproduced by a listener. The tournament scored COMPOSERS_ASSISTANT_2+CTX above REFERENCE_PART_COMPOSER on 72 % of cells; the listener preferred REFERENCE 6-4. The direction reversed. Not significant either way — which is precisely the point: the 72 % was never evidence about a human.
The context passes are inaudible here: CA2 raw vs CA2+CTX split 5-5. On the proxy the passes halved playability errors; a listener did not hear a difference in these windows.
The human anchor did not separate from the platform’s rule-based composer: HUMAN vs REFERENCE split 5-5. Against CA2+CTX the human took 7 of 10.
reading.theMethodologicalFinding: HUMAN vs REFERENCE at 5-5 is the result that matters most, and it is about the experiment rather than the composers. If real human parts are not audibly better than a deterministic rule-based part, this rendering is flattening what distinguishes them: one 8-bar window, every arm through the same reference synth, the candidate mixed forward, no performance and no production. Until the experiment can separate a human from a rule engine, it cannot be trusted to separate a trained model from an untrained one.
doNotConclude: that CA2+CTX is worse than the reference — 6-4 at n=10 is noise
that the context passes are useless — 5-5 at n=10 is noise
that the human anchor is not better — 5-5 at n=10 is noise, and the 7-3 against CA2+CTX points the other way

consequencesForThePlan: Gate C remains unpassed and unattempted: five independent raters are still required, and the owner cannot be one of them.

The decision pack’s success criterion 6 (increased human blind preference) cannot be measured at this sensitivity. Fixing the experiment now costs nothing and is a precondition for judging any training run.
Concretely: longer excerpts (a section, not eight bars), more pairs per comparison, several raters, and a rendering that does not flatten performance.
honestLimits: One rater. The owner. n = 9-10 per comparison. No result here is significant.
All 12 source tasks are classical/early music; the 840 non-classical pairs from PR-60 are unrated.
Secondary ratings were not used: the rater answered the primary question only, which is what the UX was designed to encourage.
One pair of fifty was left unanswered (contextaware_vs_ca2ctx, n = 9).
The renderer is the platform’s deterministic reference synth. It is identical for every arm, which makes the comparison fair and the absolute impression poor.
